title: First look at our 2.5D pixel MMORPG: Feedback welcome!
author: AkiraVero
selftext:
Hi everyone! My fiancée and I are making a 2.5D pixel MMORPG. We're using some AI tools to assist with developing it. The video shows beginner combat, two early boss fights and a short clip of our card game, Nine Crowns, which will be in our demo.

We'd love your feedback, especially on:

1. The camera rotation: does it belong, or is it hard on the eyes?

2. Does the combat feel satisfying, and how's the overall look?

3. Does the card game look fun and visually appealing from the short clip?



An online demo is coming soon. Our website is still a work in progress, but feel free to visit us at [https://lumoriagame.com/](https://lumoriagame.com/) Any and all feedback is greatly appreciated.



Thank you!

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Thank you! My fiancee loves cozy games while I love more nostalgic and competitive MMO's (like Ragnarok Online, Tibia) so we want to design a game that welcomes both type of players.

comments.author: Varrianda
comments.body:
Is the art AI? It looks pretty good for AI art if that’s the case.

I personally don’t like the camera rotation, feels more like a gimmick than anything. But that’s just my opinion(if I’m playing a 2d game I’d rather have the camera be static).

replies.author: iamthelobo
replies.body: Ai is getting better at assets/people are finding better methods/there's a lot of low effort art with no QA being done by the dev and no clear art direction. I'm spending a lot of time just trying to get animation right myself. I'm starting to figure some things out. I think if we put our heads together and share our tools with each other we will be able to create whatever we can dream in no time.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
The art is mainly AI with slight polishing. Once the game is more developed, we would like to hire a pixel artist to help us refine the look.

Thank you for the feedback on the camera rotation, we are very conflicted if we should keep it or not. Agree that without any clear direction, it just feels like a gimmick.

We already have character customization in our game, and we plan to have every piece of equipment be visualized. 

Here is a rough look with our terrible portraits!

https://preview.redd.it/e572gz928auh1.png?width=2082&format=png&auto=webp&s=c114ec4abdd4ab68f61ba623608ec18ba24a8f33

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body:
IMO the weakest part of your game right now is actually the player itself. The second boss looks /pretty/ good, especially for being AI art. The player almost feels a bit out of place/lacking compared to everything. The actual VFX/juice/spells aren’t bad, it’s mainly the player itself.

Also on second watch I noticed there’s collision on NPCs which might get annoying/feel clunky, but thats also a design choice and not something with a right or wrong answer

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
Thank you. I received similar feedback from a few friends playing the game where the player themselves (and the NPC's in the full game, as they are derived from the same model) look out of place compared to the world around them. We definitely need to spend more time in that area.

For collisions right now we have it set for boss monster's / MVP type of monsters. It definitely needs more testing and more design thought if it's actually needed or not and how we can incorporate that design choice into the game. 

Really appreciate all the feedback!

comments.author: HippieYoHippieYay
comments.body:
You can't call it an MMorpg until you actually get a "massive" amount of people playing it. That will never happen, sorry to pop your bubble. For reasons that we're well known even pre-AI. 

Game design and the art of game sales didn't actually change.

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body: I’m going to disagree with you. Just because no one is playing a game doesn’t change its genre. An MMO to me is a game that supports hundreds of players on screen, it doesn’t mean every second of gameplay needs hundreds of players on screen.

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body:
> The camera rotation: does it belong, or is it hard on the eyes?

My immediate question is: Why? For such a game it doesn't add anything to the gameplay. Might even be better with the fixed camera.

I'm afraid the only way to make a rotating camera work is to make the controls completely different. Like a crossover of isometric and FPS. WASD + mouse controls rotation. Fixed camera makes your game look like some generic RPG maker game that will never gain traction, so might be worth exploring other camera and/or control styles.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
Thank you for your input. Agree with your thoughts. 

When exploring the world, we feel it adds depth to the game / more immersion and has a more "uniqueness" than the fixed camera look. Like you said, with a fixed camera it looks like a generic RPG maker game and does not really stand out at all.

For controls: Currently I mainly play using WASD + mouse control rotation (holding down right mouse drags). LMB/RMB is rebind able as well as the hotbar (Can't really see it in the demo).

https://preview.redd.it/0m2mscdfqauh1.png?width=2122&format=png&auto=webp&s=4f74c8b9df41a8107f8830f68eede732cf450a93

There's also the option of using mouse movement instead of WASD and touch controls for mobile.

The problem is that during combat , theirs no real reason to rotate the camera and we rarely find ourselves using it unless we do it manually just for testing.

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> The problem is that during combat , theirs no real reason to rotate the camera and we rarely find ourselves using it 

Correct. And if no one uses it, you do a lot of work for nothing.

I kind of want to say "I have the feeling that forcing camera rotation in a not annoying way is the key to success", but I also have the feeling that constant linear rotation might not look good with pixel art. All I know is that drag-to-rotate is not the key to success.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
Thank you. I'm exploring a more Perspective look than the current Orthographic one with maybe a lower pitch. It is a very buggy and laggy build, but do you think the camera rotation would make more sense from a perspective like this? And of course, the character sprite does not really fit it in at all from this perspective and I think I'll need to spend a lot of time fixing that. Would love your thoughts 

https://reddit.com/link/per09ar/video/dfna7due4cuh1/player

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
Looks certainly a lot more unique now. 

Try that one with forced camera rotation when moving the mouse (and you shoot in the direction you look), so you make full use of you fake 3D pixel art. Just as a test. Maybe make a camera a little higher again, to better match the art perspective.
